data.cultural_impact: The name Sohrab is of Persian origin, and is renowned in the Persian epic, "The Story of Rostam and Sohrab," which is a chapter in the larger poem known as the "Shahnameh" by the Persian poet Ferdowsi. In this story, Sohrab is Rostam's son from his love affair with a noblewoman who disguised herself as a man. Sohrab grows up to become a brave and mighty warrior, unaware of his true identity as the son of Rostam. When they eventually meet on the battlefield, an emotional and tragic reunion ensues, resulting in Rostam's great sorrow. The name Sohrab has been passed down to generations, representing courage, strength, and loyalty.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Sohrab holds spiritual significance for the Muslim community, as it reflects the courage and perseverance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). During his mission to invite people to Islam, the Prophet Muhammad faced numerous challenges and adversities, displaying unwavering courage and determination in the face of opposition. The name Sohrab also reminds us of the importance of standing up for truth and justice, and striving to be a source of strength and positivity for our communities, embodying the qualities of a true Muslim.

historical_references.reference: Sohrab is believed to be the Persian hero who appears in various Persian and Indian tales, known for his extraordinary courage and valour. He is the central character in the Persian epic poem 'Sohrevardi' and in the Indian epic 'Sohrab and Rustum'. In Persian mythology, Sohrab is the son of Rustam, a legendary hero, and a Persian princess. His tragic encounter with his father during the battlefield is a popular theme in Persian and Indian literature.

The name Sohrab also appears in Islamic literature as a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). He is mentioned in several Hadiths and is believed to have embraced Islam before the Prophet's migration to Medina. Sohrab participated in the Battle of Badr and is considered a brave warrior and a devoted follower of the Prophet.
